_schema.purpose: All copy and visual specs for /solutions (index) and the nine /solutions/<slug> pages. Mirrors Lance's /solutions, /solutions/front-of-house (the 'goal' template, Lance's by-area page) and /solutions/independent (the 'brand' template, Lance's by-type page) field for field. A renderer (tools/render_solutions.py, not mine) reads this and emits src/pages/solutions/index.html and src/pages/solutions/<slug>.html.

conventions.language: British English, sentence case, full stops. 'hypjam' is always lowercase, even at the start of a sentence. Eyebrows are short labels rendered uppercase by CSS (source is sentence case).
conventions.links: Every href is a clean site URL from CONTRACT §3. Service links are NOT written inline: fields named 'service' hold an id into the top-level 'services' map, so if the services agent picked different slugs you remap them in ONE place (services.<id>.href).
conventions.arrows: Lance prefixes inline links and list titles with '↳' and card links with 'Explore →'. The glyphs are supplied by CSS (::before), not stored in copy, except where a field is literally named 'link_label'.
conventions.numbers: Every numeral on these pages is an OFFER FACT (a commitment hypjam makes) taken from hypjam-brand/pages/hire.json or CONTRACT §10. None is a result, client count or performance figure. Do not add any.
conventions.quotes: kind='founder' is the founder's own statement (Avi Aggarwal, founder, hypjam) — the single canonical statement shared with home.json, agency.json and book.json, flagged with 'sign_off': true. kind='reserved' is the held-open brand-quote slot from CONTRACT §10: same card, quote text 'The first brand quote goes here.', jam-dotted tag 'Filled in at launch'. No invented names, ever.
conventions.images: Only files that exist under assets/ are referenced. Alt text describes what is in frame. The three shoot-bay stills are named studio-*.jpg on disk; that word never appears in copy or alt text, but a naive grep of the built HTML will hit the src attribute — see 'known_risks'.

top_level.services: id → {label, href}. The nine services from CONTRACT §3 nav. Assumed slugs; remap here if the services agent chose others (CONTRACT §6 hints at short slugs like /services/casting).
top_level.platforms: The placements hypjam ships to (CONTRACT §10 replaces Lance's 'Trusted by' logo row). Rendered as monochrome typographic wordmarks we draw ourselves, opacity .5, with a trailing '+ your own site' item where Lance has '+ others'.
top_level.mocks: Named CSS/SVG mock UIs placed inside feature panels and hero panels. Referenced by id from visual.mock so one build serves every page that uses it.
top_level.pages: Nine page objects. group='goal' pages use the goal template (Lance by-area); group='brand' pages use the brand template (Lance by-type). Section order inside each object is the render order.

goal_page_fields.behind: 'The services behind it'. eyebrow, h2, p, items[] = {n:'01', service:<id>, anchor:'#brief', blurb, link_label:'Service page'}. Four columns with 1px sand-m vertical dividers, cell padding 28. Section sand-s, py 100 (max-bp: py 56).

visual_kinds.tile-icon: {kind, icon, description} — a gradient tile (layout.gradient), radius 12, with a single line icon centred (stroke #969696, 1.5px, round caps/joins, fits a 260×190 box) and a 300px hairline 'floor' under it. 'description' says what to draw; the drawing agent makes the SVG.
visual_kinds.still: {kind, src, alt, position} — an existing file under assets/img/stills or assets/video, object-cover, focal position as CSS object-position.
visual_kinds.panel: {kind, mock, ...overrides} — the sand gradient panel with a named mock from top-level 'mocks' centred in it. Overrides (message, label, rows…) replace the mock's defaults for that page.
visual_kinds.hq-drawing: {kind} — the small line drawing of hypjam's HQ (src/drawing/hq.svg at 1px stroke, whole drawing) centred in a white inner card, as Lance's footer-buildings.png.
visual_kinds.hq-room: {kind, room} — a crop of one room of the HQ drawing (room 1–5 per CONTRACT §8 bbox), rendered at 1px stroke on sand-s, object-fit contain with 48px padding. Used where Lance has a photo of a customer.
visual_kinds.reserved-phone: {kind} — the dashed-hairline frame with a line-drawn phone silhouette from CONTRACT §10, for reserved brand-story slots.

layout.grid: Two-column sections split at 50%: left column starts at the 28px gutter, right column starts at x=931 (1920 wide). Feature blocks split 780/1070 with the panel at x=821 when text-left, or the panel at x=28–1098 and text at x=1139 when text-right.
layout.gradient: linear-gradient(90deg, #e2e2e0 0%, #f5f5f5 45%, #e8e8e8 100%) — sampled from Lance's panels and tiles.
layout.eyebrow: 12px Geist, uppercase, tracking .08em, --grey, preceded by a 16px × 1px dash, 12px gap.
layout.numerals: 64px Newsreader, -1.28px tracking, black; caption 12px uppercase tracking .08em --grey, 12px below.
layout.cta: Section pb 140 (max-bp: pb 80). Card radius 16, background #dad9d4 (--sand-m), padding 48 56; left: h2 36px serif, p 16px --grey (max-width 400) mt 20, pill button mt 96 (pill on sand: rgba(0,0,0,.06) bg, black text, black arrow circle); right: white inner card radius 12, 895×360, the hq-drawing centred at ~520px wide.
layout.h1_widths: Measured with the shipped Newsreader at 64px/1.05/-1.28px: every goal-page h1 here sets 3 lines at max-width 540 (Lance's own by-area h1 does the same at that width); every brand-page h1 sets 2 lines centred at max-width 640 (as Lance's); the index h1 sets 2 lines at 700 (Lance's index h1 needs a wider box, ~750). Facts captions all fit one line at 12px uppercase tracking .08em in a 600px column.
layout.buttons: Lance's pill (CONTRACT §4): height 32, 14px, gap 10, padding-left 16, trailing 22px circle. On white the pill is #efefef with a black circle and white arrow; on dark it is rgba(255,255,255,.12) with a --jam circle and black arrow.
layout.mobile: ≤1024: every grid becomes one column, panels go full width at aspect 4:3, facts stack with 48px gaps, the hero panel sits under the copy, section paddings per CONTRACT §4 (80px).

known_risks: Service hrefs are assumed slugs; confirm against content/services.json when it exists.

assets/img/stills/studio-*.jpg file names contain 'studio'. The word never appears in copy or alt text here, but a grep of built HTML will hit the src attribute; the asset owner may want to rename them (e.g. bay-*.jpg) and update the 'src' fields below.
Founder quotes are the founder's single canonical statement (identical to home.json quotes.items[0].text); each is flagged sign_off: true.

conversation.size: fits a 1070×715 panel; group centred, ~480 wide
conversation.spec: Top row: a 20px line phone-handset icon and a 14px --grey caption '{sender}'. Below it a white speech bubble (radius 16, 1px sand-m border, shadow 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.08), padding 14 18, 16px black text, 300px wide, tail bottom-left) containing '{message}'. A 1.5px --sand-l curved connector runs from the bubble's right edge to a black rounded square (84×84, radius 20) holding /assets/brand/logos/hypjam-icon.svg at 44px; under the square a 16px/500 black label '{label}'. Loop: the bubble fades and slides in (0.6s), the connector draws (0.5s), the square scales from .9 (0.4s), hold 3s, reset.

brief-card.size: 420×300 white card, radius 12, 1px sand-m, shadow 0 12px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.06)
brief-card.spec: Header 13px --grey 'Brief · your brand' with a 6px --jam dot and 'in progress' right-aligned. Five rows (14px, label --grey left, value black right, 1px sand-s rules): Product · 'the serum' | Goal · 'launch, March' | Platforms · three chips TikTok · Reels · Shorts (chip: 12px, 1px sand-m, radius 999) | Budget band · 'growth' | Hooks · '8'. Rows type in one at a time (0.35s each), hold 3s, reset.

hook-list.spec: Eight rows: 12px --grey number '01'–'08' then a 14px black hook line. Lines: 'I did not expect this to actually work' · 'Stop scrolling if your skin does this in winter' · 'POV: you finally read the ingredients' · 'The one product I did not post until it worked' · 'Three things nobody tells you about serums' · 'I switched and nobody noticed. That is the point' · 'Wait for the second bottle' · 'My dermatologist friend asked what this was'. Rows type in at 0.3s each; then rows 02 and 07 get a --jam tick and a 12px 'picked for the shoot' tag; hold 3s; reset.

casting-board.size: three cards 150×200 in a row, gap 20, white, radius 12, 1px sand-m
casting-board.spec: Each card: a 56px line-drawn avatar circle (stroke #969696 1.5px, simple head and shoulders), a 14px black handle '@—' (three dashes, no real names), and three 12px --grey tags 'skincare · 25–34 · London' / 'home · 35–44 · Leeds' / 'fitness · 18–24 · remote'. Cards slide in from the right 0.4s apart; the middle card lifts 8px and gets a --jam 'shortlisted' tag; hold 3s; reset.

phone-rec.size: phone frame 280×580, radius 40, 8px white bezel, screen sand-s; take list 220 wide to its right
phone-rec.spec: Top-left of the screen: a 8px --jam dot pulsing at 1Hz next to 12px 'REC 00:12:07' (timecode runs). At 70% height a caption bar (black, radius 6, 13px white) 'wait for the second hook'. Take list (14px): 'hook 03 — take 1' struck through --grey, 'hook 03 — take 2 ✓' black with a --jam tick, 'hook 05 — take 1' pending. Every 4s the tick moves down one line.

timeline.spec: Three tracks (labels 12px --grey: video · captions · sound). Video track: four clip blocks (sand-m, radius 4) with 12px labels 'hook' 'demo' 'proof' 'cta'. Captions track: a 'CC' toggle in --jam, on. Sound track: a low waveform stroke. A 1px --jam playhead scrubs left to right over 3s. Under the tracks an export bar (4px, sand-m) fills --jam over 1.2s, then three 12px labels light in --jam with ticks: TikTok · Reels · Shorts. Hold 2s; reset.

spark-toggle.spec: Tabs 'TikTok' (active, 1px black underline) and 'Meta' (--grey). Row: 40px line avatar + '@—' handle + 12px --grey 'creator'. Row: 14px 'Authorise for Spark Ads' with a toggle (44×24) that flips to --jam. Row: 14px 'Ad code' with a dotted field '••••-••••' that fills to 'ready' in --jam. Loop 5s.

rights-sheet.spec: Title 14px black 'Usage rights · your brand × @—'. Rows 14px (label --grey, value black): Organic · ✓ | Paid · ✓ | Whitelisting · ✓ | Window · '6 months' | Territory · 'UK'. Bottom: a signature line (1px sand-m) with a 12px 'signed before the shoot' label and a --jam circle stamp (28px) that scales in at the end. Loop 5s.

report-grid.size: 3×3 grid, cells 100×70, gap 6, inside a 420×300 white card
report-grid.spec: Column headers 12px --grey 'hook 02 · hook 07 · hook 05'; row headers '@— · @— · @—'. Cells are sand-s and shade to sand-m/sand-l one by one (no numbers anywhere); one cell gets a 1.5px --jam outline and a 12px 'run this' tag. Footer 12px --grey: 'next brief: two more like hook 07'. Loop 6s.

founder-take.size: phone frame 240×500 (as phone-rec) plus a 260-wide prompt card to its right
founder-take.spec: On the phone screen a simple line-drawn person (head, shoulders, one hand up holding a product box) and a caption bar 'take 3'. The prompt card (white, radius 12): 12px --grey 'Hook' then 16px black 'It took two years to get the lid right.' then 12px --grey 'Say it to the lens, not the notes.' Every 4s the caption goes 'take 4' and the card's hook line swaps to 'Nobody asked for this. We made it anyway.'

trend-board.spec: Three rows, each: a 60×24 waveform stroke (#969696), 14px black 'sound 01/02/03', 12px --grey 'moving this week' with a --jam up-arrow on row 2 only. Right of the rows a 120×214 mini phone frame showing a 'stitched' split screen (two sand-m blocks). Row 2 gets a 12px 'brief sent' chip in --jam. Loop 5s.

retention-flow.spec: Three nodes (white, radius 12, 1px sand-m, 150×90) joined by 1.5px --sand-l arrows: 'Order' → 'Day 3 · how-to video' → 'Day 21 · reorder'. Each video node carries a --jam play triangle (12px). Arrows draw left to right (0.5s each), then the middle node's triangle pulses. Loop 5s.

meta.title: Launches: hooks, casting and cuts before the product ships | hypjam
meta.description: How hypjam runs a product launch: a brief on a call, eight hooks per script, creators cast from our roster and approved by you, a phone shoot, and first cuts inside fourteen days, cleared for organic and paid.

hero.h1: A launch with its hooks written before it ships
hero.intro: hypjam takes the brief on a call, writes the hooks, casts the creators, directs the shoot and delivers first cuts inside fourteen days, cleared for organic and paid. Your team keeps the launch.

visual.message: We are launching the serum in March. Can we have hooks by the 20th?
visual.label: Briefing & scripts

facts.h2: Most launch content is briefed too late. Every part of this one is briefed first.
facts.p: On hypjam the script is locked before anyone films and the creators are cast before the product lands. Four services make that happen, in the order a launch actually needs them.

items.label: From a signed brief to your first cuts
TikTok, Reels, Shorts, Snap, Pinterest and Meta, cut natively

behind.p: Each one is a service on its own. Together they cover what happens before the shoot, on the shoot, and in the fortnight before the launch date.

items.blurb: Turns a call into a brief with a product, a goal, a date and a budget band.
Writes eight hooks per script and picks the ones worth filming.
Casts from our own roster for the product, and shows you the shortlist.
Cuts each take for the placement it is going to, captions burned in.

features.h2: The brief is written on the first call, in your words.
features.p: hypjam starts with a conversation, not an order form. What the product is, who it is for, what the launch date is, what you have already tried. By the end of the call the brief is on the tracker with a budget band and a date, and nothing is guessed.

points.title: One brief, not a vibe
points.body: The brief carries the product, the offer, the platforms, the tone and the date. It is the document the writer, the producer and the editor all work from, so the creator's take matches what you asked for.

points.title: A budget band, not a mystery
points.body: Packages start from £1,800 a month and the brief says which one fits. 'From' is honest: the final number is scoped once we know how many videos you need and how long you want the rights for.

points.title: Tracked live
points.body: Every brief sits on a live tracker you can open. Casting, scripting, shooting and editing move across it during the sprint, so you never have to ask where things are.

features.h2: Eight hooks are written before anyone presses record.
features.p: The first three seconds decide whether the rest of the video is watched, so that is where the writing time goes. Every script starts as eight hooks of different kinds: curiosity, comparison, POV, a plain claim. Two or three are picked for the shoot. The rest are kept for round two.

points.title: Hooks of different kinds
points.body: A launch does not know which angle will land, so the eight are deliberately different: a question, a confession, a comparison, a 'wait for it'. The shoot covers more than one so the ad account has something to choose between.

points.title: Scripted, then loosened
points.body: Each hook has a one-line script and a payoff. Creators get the script and the direction, and deliver it in their own timing and words. Directed, not read.

points.title: Kept for the next round
points.body: The hooks that did not make the shoot stay in the brief. When the first cuts have run, the next round starts from what is already written.

features.h2: Casting is from our roster, and you approve the shortlist.
features.p: Creators are cast from hypjam's own roster for tone, look and niche, not follower count. You see the shortlist before anyone shoots. The creator gets the brief, the script and the references, so they arrive knowing what the launch is for.

points.title: Cast for the product
points.body: Skincare, home, fitness, food, tech, parenting: the roster is organised by what people actually use and film. A launch is cast for the person your customer would believe, not the biggest account.

points.title: You see who, first
points.body: The shortlist lands on the tracker with each creator's handle and previous work. Nobody films until you have said yes.

points.title: Paid by us, once
points.body: Creators are paid out of your package fee on a set schedule. One contract, one invoice, no separate negotiations on your side.

features.h2: Each take is cut for the placement it is going to.
features.p: A TikTok cut and a Reels cut are not the same file with a different export. The editor cuts for how each feed is watched: pacing, captions, sound, where the product first appears. Captions are burned in and kept clear of the platform's own overlays.

points.title: Native, not resized
points.body: Every video is cut 9:16 for the platform it is going to, with the hook in the first frame and the caption inside the safe area. Six placements, six cuts if the brief needs them.

points.title: One revision round, included
points.body: Every package includes one full revision round per video. Most rounds get used on pacing or captions rather than reshoots, because the script was locked before anyone filmed.

points.title: Delivered with a note
points.body: The cuts arrive with the usage rights and our read on what to run where. Then we watch what performs and brief the next round around it.

problems.h2: Built for the problems a launch actually has.
problems.p: Not a marketplace with a search box. hypjam is built around the launch date that will not move, the one hero film with no variants, and the rights that are not sorted the day the ad has to go live.

how.h2: From the first call to the first cuts.

steps.title: The brief lands
steps.body: A thirty-minute call. Product, goal, date, budget band, and what you have already tried. It is on the tracker the same day.

steps.title: Hooks and scripts
steps.body: Eight hooks per script, each with a one-line payoff. You pick with us which ones go to the shoot.

steps.title: Cast and shot
steps.body: Creators are cast from the roster and approved by you, then directed through the takes on their own phones.

hood.h2: On a phone, from a script, under a contract.
hood.p: The details a marketing lead asks about before signing a launch brief.

items.label: Turnaround
items.body: From a signed brief to first cuts. Casting, shooting and editing all happen inside the sprint, tracked live.

items.label: Hooks
items.body: Every script starts as eight hooks. Two or three are picked for the shoot; the rest are kept for the next round.

items.label: Casting
items.body: Creators come from our own roster, cast for the product. Nobody shoots until you have seen the shortlist.

items.q: Do creators need to come to London?
items.a: No. The roster is mostly remote: food shoots happen in the creator's own kitchen, directed over a call. A London shoot with the director in the room can be arranged when the product needs a clean counter and a close-up pour.

items.q: How do you handle health and nutrition claims?
items.a: Hooks are written so the line on screen is one the product can stand behind under the CAP Code, and we would rather cut a line than get you a letter. Paid partnerships are labelled where the platform requires it.

items.a: Up to five formats from one shoot: taste test, recipe, unboxing, reaction and testimonial, each cut native for its placement. A Starter month is six videos; Growth is twelve.
